title: Dub 201 Control (019)
notes: THE CONTROL. 019 as it is: the same kits, the same patches, the same room, the same sends, the same six modulators. The one deliberate difference is F's CHORD, 3 in 019 and 0 here - see the voices block. Everything the other nineteen change, they change against this.

0.why: four on the floor, the anchor - 019's own kick placement

1.why: backbeat on two and four, dry

2.why: one clap a bar, drenched - the step the delay modulator opens on

3.why: offbeat sixteenths, the hat that breathes

5.why: 019's bass figure, note for note: steps 0, 6, 10 and 14 off register 58. CHORD IS 0 HERE AND 3 IN 019, and that is the one musical change the round makes to the control's neighbours: a triad down at the bass octave is mud, the third source asks for 'a sub bass that barely moves', and a bass playing three notes would make every engine comparison a comparison of how well a patch handles a low triad. random and rhythm are 0 so the line is the SAME line in all twenty - owner's instruction 2026-09-12, 'keep melodys fixed in the first place'.

6.why: G plays CHORDS, which the generator cannot write - see the chords block. This entry is not what sounds; it is the octave the pads colour against, and what the generator would write on steps 6 and 14 if ownership were ever handed back.

7.why: H is a deep pad: ONE chord a bar, held almost the whole bar. Like G it is authored as a take, so this entry is the octave the pads colour against.

4.why: E is silent in this variant. `empty` is rhythm_reg 0: the mask is all zero, no note is written, and the pads draw an empty line. Said explicitly rather than by leaving the channel out, because a drum pattern is NOT rewritten on load - an absent block leaves 018's own leftover line playing.

6.why: G minor - G3 Bb3 D4 - on the and of beat 2
the flat-seventh chord voiced up, A3 C4 F4, on the and of beat 4. i to bVII is the dub progression, and this voicing keeps all three notes inside the pad keyboard

7.why: G minor voiced open and low - G2 D3 Bb3, root, fifth, tenth - one chord a bar held 15 of 16 steps, which is 1.9 s at 120 BPM. The tenth rather than a close third so it does not crowd the bass, and the one-step gap before the retrigger keeps the note clear of the loop wrap.

6.name: BzSYN PolySynth
6.why: 019's own BASS patch, and the control variant exists to be 019: it is kept here EXACTLY as 019 ships it, octave 0.25 and tune 0.608 included. Those two are not centred - read out of the .ttl on the rig 2026-09-12 - so this patch plays a little under its written pitch. That is what the owner has been hearing since 2026-09-05 and the control must reproduce it, not correct it. Every OTHER variant's bass patch was chosen with octave 0.5 and tune 0.5 so the twenty share a pitch.  voicecount forced to 1.0 - EIGHT voices - and unison off. Every Obxd patch in this pack ships voicecount 0.25, which is between the scale points for two and three voices, and a three-note chord on a two-voice patch loses a note in silence. unison stacks voices per NOTE, so it spends the polyphony a chord needs. Nothing else is overridden: the restore writes saved controllers OVER the preset, so a fourth value here would be the old patch winning against the new one.

8.name: TapeStrings
8.why: 019's own PADS patch. DCA1_ATTACK 0.14, DCA1_RELEASE 0.56, DCF1_CUTOFF 0.72 - the swell the factory snapshot ships.  DEF1_MONO is 0 in this patch, read out of its own .ttl on the rig - a padthv1 patch with DEF1_MONO 1 collapses a chord to one note and says nothing. No controller is forced: the patch is wanted as it is.

mods.why: a 16-bar breath on the kick
the snare tail opens and closes over eight bars
the clap echo comes and goes over six bars - the dub move
the hats breathe against everything else over four bars
the stab's echo swells and recedes over three bars
and its room opens and closes over eight, out of phase with the echo

mods_why: THE SIX MODULATORS ARE IDENTICAL IN ALL TWENTY, and that is the point: the round varies instrumentation and effects, so everything else is held still. Their BASES are not written here - the builder reads each one back off the mixer strip or the insert wet this same run wrote, which is why a variant that moves a send automatically moves the modulator that sweeps around it. Every target is `level`, `reverb` or `delay`: a mixer fader and the two TAP inserts, none of which is GUI-hosted. A modulator pointed at a plugin Zynthian hosts in jalv.gtk3 costs about 70 % of a core per instance (notes/traps/PLUGINS.md), and eight of the twelve effects this project uses are GUI-hosted - which is the whole reason the insert pair is never swapped in this round.
levels_why: THE EIGHT CHANNEL FADERS ARE 019'S, UNCHANGED, IN ALL TWENTY - every ratio the owner tuned by ear on 2026-09-02 is held, so what differs between the twenty is the patches and the sends and not the balance. THE MAIN FADER IS MEASURED, and it is the only number in the mix that moves between variants. Read on the rig 2026-09-12 over FORTY-EIGHT BARS - the LCM of the six modulator periods, and the window snapshot/README.md insists on after a 10-bar read of 019 came back 3.6 dB low - on zynmixer:output_17a with the transport running: this variant read rms -23.51 dBFS and peak -9.31, and 0.28 x 1.091 = 0.3056 brings it to the round's common -22.75 dBFS. THE ROOM IS WHY THE TRIM EXISTS: TAP Reverberator's forty-three modes do not share an output gain, so choosing a room moves the whole bus by several dB - and a listening round where the loudest variant wins has taught nothing. The ceiling is -3 dBFS of predicted peak; the target is pulled down to whatever satisfies it, so no variant is trimmed into clipping.

6.why: 019 swapped F from JC303 to Obxd on 2026-09-02 and the round keeps it: the bass patch is chosen by reading, and JC303 publishes no preset bundle to read.

title: Dub 219 Glitch Percussion
notes: THE FIFTH CHANNEL BECOMES GLITCH PERCUSSION. E keeps its LinuxSampler kit and is switched to behave as a VOICE, so the Turing register walks it: each step picks a DIFFERENT SAMPLE out of the 808 rather than a pitch, which is the 'glitch percussion' the second source builds after the kick. The register is fixed - random and rhythm both 0 - so it is the same four sounds every bar.

0.why: four on the floor, the anchor - 019's own kick placement

1.why: backbeat on two and four, dry

2.why: one clap a bar, drenched - the step the delay modulator opens on

3.why: offbeat sixteenths, the hat that breathes

4.why: E IS IN BOTH `drums` AND `voices` ON PURPOSE, and the order the builder runs them in is what makes it work: the drums step is here only to choose the KIT, and the voices step then replaces the pattern it wrote. Without this entry E would keep whatever kit 018 happens to carry.

5.why: 019's bass figure, note for note: steps 0, 6, 10 and 14 off register 58. CHORD IS 0 HERE AND 3 IN 019, and that is the one musical change the round makes to the control's neighbours: a triad down at the bass octave is mud, the third source asks for 'a sub bass that barely moves', and a bass playing three notes would make every engine comparison a comparison of how well a patch handles a low triad. random and rhythm are 0 so the line is the SAME line in all twenty - owner's instruction 2026-09-12, 'keep melodys fixed in the first place'.

6.why: G plays CHORDS, which the generator cannot write - see the chords block. This entry is not what sounds; it is the octave the pads colour against, and what the generator would write on steps 6 and 14 if ownership were ever handed back.

7.why: H is a deep pad: ONE chord a bar, held almost the whole bar. Like G it is authored as a take, so this entry is the octave the pads colour against.

4.why: steps 2, 5, 9 and 13 - none of them on a beat - off register 179 at octave 0, which lands in the 40s and 50s. Every note from 36 to 60 is mapped in the TR808 .sfz (read on the rig 2026-09-12), so none of the four is a silent step. range 2 spreads them over two octaves' worth of the kit instead of one.

6.why: G minor - G3 Bb3 D4 - on the and of beat 2
the flat-seventh chord voiced up, A3 C4 F4, on the and of beat 4. i to bVII is the dub progression, and this voicing keeps all three notes inside the pad keyboard

7.why: G minor voiced open and low - G2 D3 Bb3, root, fifth, tenth - one chord a bar held 15 of 16 steps, which is 1.9 s at 120 BPM. The tenth rather than a close third so it does not crowd the bass, and the one-step gap before the retrigger keeps the note clear of the loop wrap.

6.name: Synth Bass 1 OB-Xd
6.why: cutoff 0.20, resonance 0.136, decay 0.336, sustain 0.116: a short dark sub that barely moves, which is what the third source asks a dub bass for. octave 0.5 and tune 0.5, so it plays the written key.  voicecount forced to 1.0 - EIGHT voices - and unison off. Every Obxd patch in this pack ships voicecount 0.25, which is between the scale points for two and three voices, and a three-note chord on a two-voice patch loses a note in silence. unison stacks voices per NOTE, so it spends the polyphony a chord needs. Nothing else is overridden: the restore writes saved controllers OVER the preset, so a fourth value here would be the old patch winning against the new one.

8.why: 019's own PADS patch. DCA1_ATTACK 0.14, DCA1_RELEASE 0.56, DCF1_CUTOFF 0.72 - the swell the factory snapshot ships.
